public_rationale: The October reporting documents financing stress and continuing deal activity. It does not clearly establish the broad AI investment bust required by the forecast. Treating that pullback as the trigger would make the result depend on an evaluator-supplied definition. With the antecedent unknown, the conditional forecast cannot yet be scored.
limitations: A narrower definition of bust could classify the October events differently.
Continuing deals are not decisive without establishing both the trigger and new commitment dates.
The absence of a deadline prevents treating a temporary funding interruption as final confirmation.

statement.excerpt: Once the bubble bursts, any excitement for AI — and by extension excitement to spend money on AI — goes out the window. AI startups won’t get funded. AI token budgets won’t get greenlit. AI data centers won’t be able to raise debt.

from_speaker: AI token budgets won’t get greenlit
AI data centers won’t be able to raise debt
our_interpretation: The antecedent is a recognizable broad AI investment bust, not merely one failed company, a regional setback, or a short selloff.
No numerical crash threshold is invented because the speaker supplied none.
The three predictions are categorical statements about new funding, new budget approvals, and new debt after that bust.
Closing a financing committed before the bust would not by itself establish renewed post-bust funding availability.
This is a qualitative claim about market access, not a stated financial amount for an identified company.
criteria.support_condition: After an independently established AI investment bust, sufficiently comprehensive evidence shows new AI startup financing, token-budget approvals, and AI data-center debt all cease. A finite interruption alone cannot establish an indefinite categorical ban.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the bust is independently established and dated, a verified new AI startup financing, approved token budget, or AI data-center debt commitment contradicts the corresponding categorical prediction.
